H1_synthetic_data_fidelity.note: Classical GAN-LLM has ONE run, so a two-sample test is impossible. This Crawford-Howell test asks whether that single run lies outside the spread of QGAN-LLM; it is exploratory, not confirmatory.
H1_synthetic_data_fidelity.note_covariate: no usable 'vix' covariate (or < 2 runs per side) in results/all_results.csv -- ran a plain comparison instead of the ANCOVA Ch.3 specifies

H3_poisoning_resistance.note: no_noise has ONE run, so a two-sample test is impossible. This Crawford-Howell test asks whether that single run lies outside the spread of noisy; it is exploratory, not confirmatory.
H3_poisoning_resistance.confound_warning: noisy = 20-qubit ring + 12-qubit + linear-topology configs pooled; they differ from no_noise in more than the noise level only
H3_poisoning_resistance.interpretation: positive t (no_noise mean > noisy mean) supports Ha3: noise injection -> lower poisoning degradation

rmse.reason: all 5 observations are identical (value=0.000612877); the quantity does not depend on the model under test, so no test statistic exists
rmse.why: In QGAN-LLM and Classical GAN-LLM the forecast head is a linear layer fitted in closed form on REAL rows only; the generator is never on the forecast path. More seeds cannot create a difference. A quantum-vs-classical RMSE/ASR comparison needs the generator (or its output) to feed the forecast -- see the Ch.4 diagnosis.
